subject: Mutual action plan: hosting-mode decision & region acceptance gates

Cc: ops@medtech.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft MAP & decision cadence — hosting mode + region windows

Hi Katie —

Thanks for the time last week. Per our conversation I've attached a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) draft and an evaluation checklist that maps acceptance gates to the hosting-mode options (Hosted, Dedicated, Private). The objective here is simple: align on decision criteria and a pragmatic timeline so your engineering and procurement teams can close the hosting-mode and region choice during the POC sprint.

Quick summary of asks for next steps:
- Please review the attached MAP and mark any missing acceptance criteria (security, latency SLO, data residency).
- Confirm whether a procurement/contract review window is required before legal signature (procurement@medtech.ai copied).
- Tentative recommendation from our side: run a 2-week hosted POC for feature parity + a 1-week Dedicated performance verification in us-east; Private will be scoped only if there are hard on-prem/regulatory constraints.

I propose we lock the MAP during a 30-minute sync on Wednesday. If that works, send a preferred time and I'll send the invite + a short agenda: acceptance gates, cutover cadence, and pricing envelope scenarios.

Attachments: MedTech_MAP_draft_20270315.pdf (MAP draft), eval-checklist-templates.xlsx (acceptance gates)

Thanks,
Camila

Camila —

Thanks for sending this over, the MAP looks like a good starting point. A couple of clarifying items from our side before the sync:
- Data residency: our legal team flagged that patient-identifiable metadata in PII-adjacent logs must stay in the US. Is the Hosted option guaranteed to keep logs in the selected region, or do we need Dedicated/Private to meet log-residency requirements?
- Private: can you clarify what the typical timeline and cost delta are for a Private on-prem deployment vs. Dedicated? Our procurement lead (copied) needs rough numbers to plan budget windows.

We can do Wednesday 10:30am PT for the 30-minute sync. If you can share a short one-pager on residency guarantees and the Private timeline estimate before then, that would help us align internally.

Best,

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Draft MAP & decision cadence — hosting mode + region windows

Katie —

Appreciate the quick review. Short answers up front, and we'll walk the details in Wednesday's sync (10:30am PT).

Resident logs: Hosted API keeps customer data in the selected region and we surface region-level retention and export controls. For absolute guarantees around audit evidence and KMS separation we recommend Dedicated (customer-dedicated GPU pool with isolated storage) or Private (VPC/on-prem). I'll attach a one-page residency note in the meeting thread — it highlights what we cover in Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.

Private timeline & delta (high-level):
- Private (on-prem/VPC): Typical lead time 8–12 weeks for on-prem packaging + security review; capital/eng setup cost varies widely (we'll provide a notch estimate).
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): 2–4 weeks to provision reserved pools and run a performance verification window; lower up-front cost than Private and similar SLA guardrails.

Proposed MAP milestones (high level):
1) Week 0: MAP sign-off (acceptance gates finalized)
2) Weeks 1–2: Hosted POC (feature parity + latency baseline)
3) Weeks 3–4: Dedicated performance verification (if chosen) or canary in Hosted with KV caching enabled
4) Week 5: Acceptance gate review and go/no-go for cutover

I've uploaded the residency one-pager and a base budget envelope to the shared drive: https://drive.redwood.com/medtech/MAP-2027-03-15 (see "Residency_OnePager.pdf" and "Budget_Envelope_Deltas.xlsx").

See you Wednesday — I'll send calendar invite in a minute.

—Camila
Camila Reyes
Senior Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference

Camila / team —

Thanks for the run-through; the MAP looks good and aligns with our internal calendar. After talking with procurement, MedTech is electing to proceed with Dedicated reserved capacity in us-east as the target deployment path. The rationale: we need regionally-resident logs + predictable throughput for next quarter's clinical pilot, but we want to avoid the multi-week on-prem lead time for Private.

Requested next steps from our side:
- Please share an updated MAP with the Dedicated timeline baked in (2–4 week provisioning) and a provisional SOW stub so procurement can start internal approvals.
- We want a canary/cutover window target: start Dedicated verification on 2027-04-05 with a 7-day verification period; go/no-go review on 2027-04-12.

Attachments: SOW_medtech_signed_stub.pdf (procurement asked for a stub to start approvals; final SOW pending legal)

We'll await the updated MAP and SOW.
